basis: CF, gastritis and anemia define syndrome; intellectual disability 80-99%. H. pylori infection and renal disease (30-79%) omitted under four-axis cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: cystic fibrosis defines the syndrome and causes intrinsic airway disease; recurrent respiratory infections occur in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%; retained for its common, substantial neurodevelopmental impairment.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: defining H. pylori infection qualifies, but the four-axis cap prioritizes pulmonary, gastrointestinal, haematologic and neurologic damage.

basis: Restrictive skin and congenital contractures define disease; ankylosis 7/7 and bone defects 5/5. Pulmonary hypoplasia affects most patients and contributes to neonatal lethality.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: fixed congenital contractures are defining; ankylosis occurs in 7/7 and distal phalangeal osteolysis in 5/5.

basis: Global developmental delay 30-79%, despite conflicting rare annotation. Bronchiectasis is a separate infection sequela; intestinal hyperplasia lacks common functional injury.

decisions.haematologic: none: immune-cell abnormalities and lymphoproliferation do not establish a separate blood disorder or impaired splenic blood function.
decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis is reported in 30-79%, but represents a separately diagnosed sequela of recurrent infections rather than direct intrinsic lung injury.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: intestinal lymphoid hyperplasia occurs in 30-79%, but functional injury is not established; diarrhea and malabsorption are only 5-29%.

basis: Defining platelet dysfunction/asplenia, myopathy and ichthyosis (80-99%). Characteristic dyslexia and speech abnormalities (80-99%) support neurologic involvement; miosis lacks functional injury.

decisions.neurologic: involved: characteristic dyslexia and speech abnormalities (80-99%) support neurodevelopmental dysfunction; migraine alone would not qualify.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent ichthyosis is explicitly part of the defining syndrome and occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Mitochondrial disorder; brain abnormalities/seizures, cardiomyopathy and muscle weakness each reported in 1/1. Ophthalmoplegia/ptosis omitted under four-axis cap; denominators are small.

decisions.ocular: none: ophthalmoplegia and ptosis occur in 1/1, but ocular involvement is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of brain, heart and broader muscle disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: mitochondrial muscle dysfunction with weakness occurs in 1/1; prioritized over ocular motor manifestations under the cap.

basis: Hyperandrogenism defines endocrine disease; frontal balding represents hair loss in 80-99%. Renal agenesis is occasional (5-29%) overall despite an isolated 1/1 annotation.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: frontal balding is direct hair loss, reported in 80-99%; hirsutism alone would not establish tissue damage.

basis: Nephrotic FSGS and congenital hydrocephalus define organ disease. Blue sclerae and thin skin lack documented functional impairment.

decisions.ocular: none: blue sclerae are a descriptive color change without documented visual impairment or damaging ocular disease.

basis: Contractures, muscle hypoplasia, blepharophimosis and palatal defects define syndrome. Neurodevelopmental impairment and microcephaly occur in 80-99%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: palatal clefts are explicitly defining structural oral abnormalities; submucous cleft palate occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay, learning disability and microcephaly occur in 80-99%; three primary slots retain defining musculoskeletal, eyelid and palatal disease.

basis: Immune-mediated skin and mucosal necrosis; destructive oral mucositis occurs in >90%. Damaging ocular findings are 5-29%; cytopenias may reflect drugs or sepsis.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: destruction of mucous membranes is explicitly defining; oral mucosal necrosis occurs in >90%, placing the mouth on the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; acute hepatic failure and progressive neurologic deterioration each occur in 1/2 (~50%). Isolated ptosis does not establish intrinsic ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis occurs in 1/2, but this isolated sign does not establish visual impairment or intrinsic ocular damage.
